To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have produced a functional rat PDI in yeast, and that this protein is indistinguishable from the mammalian protein in its catalytic activity.
rat protein disulfides isomerase was produced in Saccharomyes cerevisiae, and that the yeast protein was indistinguishable in its catalytic activity from the mammalian protein.

we have developed a method for the production of rat protein disulphide isomerase, a protein that is required for the viability of yeast, by expressing the gene for this protein in yeast, and have demonstrated that the yeast-produced protein has the same properties as the protein that is normally produced in rat.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of rat protein disulphide isomerase.
the expression and purification of PDI from yeast and its characterization.
the production of a recombinant protein in a eukaryotic expression system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the yeast PDI is a functional homolog of the mammalian PDI.
the yeast cells are able to secrete the rat PDI into the medium, and the protein is able to function in the yeast cells.

PDI is an essential component of a complex that is involved in the folding and assembly of secretory and membrane proteins in eukaryotic cells, and that the protein disulfide bond isomerization and/or reduction activity is essential for this function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have produced rat protein disulfidase in yeast.
the expression of a heterologous protein in yeast can be achieved by using a yeast promoter, a yeast signal sequence, and an ER retention signal.
the expression system described here is unique in allowing both the same plasmids to be used both for the complementation and production of PDI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it should be possible to express a wide variety of proteins in yeast and to purify the resulting products.
it is possible to express rat PDI in S. cerevisae, and that the protein is secreted and has the catalytic activity of PDI from bovine liver.
the expression of rat PDI in S. cerevisiea is a very effective and convenient way to obtain large amounts of PDI for in vitro studies of its structure, function, and interactions.
